summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, was admitted for symptomatic in-stent restenosis of the renal artery to his transplanted kidney. He presented with elevated blood pressure, and a transplant kidney ultrasound revealed significantly increased renal artery velocities, confirming restenosis. He underwent elective angioplasty of the existing renal artery stent, which was performed successfully without complications. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with no change in kidney function post-procedure. His pain was controlled, and he tolerated a diet advance. He was discharged home in stable condition on day two with continued immunosuppressive, antihypertensive, and antiplatelet therapy, and instructions to follow up with vascular surgery in two weeks.
